title: NFL’s 0‑2 Teams Still Alive: Texans, Buccaneers & Colts Keep Playoff Dreams Alive in Week 3
body:
The NFL’s early‑season leaderboard is already shaping up like a roller‑coaster, but four of the league’s eight winless clubs still have a realistic path to the postseason as they head into Week 3. In a fresh ranking, NFL.com analyst Kevin Patra evaluated the Houston Texans, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Indianapolis Colts and a handful of other 0‑2 teams, highlighting why youth, coaching changes and schedule quirks keep their playoff dreams alive despite two early defeats.

The Texans sit atop the list, largely because of the unprecedented growth of their rookie quarterback, C.J. Stroud. After a rough opening loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, Stroud’s poise in the second half of a 23‑20 defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars demonstrated a rapid learning curve that could translate into wins against the less formidable opponents on the remaining schedule. Houston’s revamped offensive line, bolstered by free‑agent signings, has also shown signs of cohesion, limiting sacks and giving Stroud the time needed to develop his rhythm. Patra notes that if the Texans can maintain a sub‑30‑second defensive third‑down conversion rate, they could realistically finish the season above .500 and sneak into the wild‑card picture.

Tampa Bay, despite a bruising loss to the New England Patriots and a narrow defeat at the hands of the New York Giants, remains a contender thanks to a rejuvenated defense and the emergence of rookie wide receiver Jaelon Darden. The Buccaneers’ secondary, now anchored by veteran safety Jordan Whitehead, has cut down big plays, while the front seven has increased its pressure rate to a league‑average 35 percent. Coach Todd Bowles’ aggressive play‑calling has also sparked a more dynamic offense, with quarterback Baker Mayfield showing flashes of accuracy that could be enough to capitalize on the favorable remaining matchups against the Detroit Lions and Carolina Panthers.

The Indianapolis Colts, though still searching for their first win, have a schedule that could turn their fortunes around quickly. After a lopsided loss to the Baltimore Ravens and a close contest with the Cleveland Browns, the Colts’ young offensive line and the steady development of quarterback Anthony Richardson are beginning to click. Richardson’s dual‑threat ability has already produced several big plays, and with the addition of veteran running back Jonathan Taylor, Indianapolis possesses a balanced attack that could exploit the defensive vulnerabilities of upcoming opponents like the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Houston Texans. Patra emphasizes that a single win in the next two weeks would not only boost morale but also keep the Colts within striking distance of a playoff berth, given the AFC’s historically volatile mid‑season standings.

Other 0‑2 squads, such as the New York Jets and the Denver Broncos, face steeper odds. The Jets’ defense, while improving, still struggles against the pass, and quarterback Aaron Rodgers’ lingering injury concerns limit the team’s offensive upside. Denver’s offensive line woes and a turnover‑prone secondary make a late‑season surge unlikely, though a favorable schedule could still provide a glimmer of hope. Patra places these teams lower in his ranking, noting that their path to the playoffs would require a combination of health, drastic performance upgrades and a string of favorable outcomes in other divisions.

What unites the four hopefuls is a common narrative of growth and adaptation. Young players are gaining valuable experience at a faster pace than anticipated, and coaching staffs are making adjustments that appear to be bearing fruit. The early-season losses, while discouraging, have offered a clear diagnostic tool for teams to identify weaknesses and address them before the schedule tightens. Moreover, the NFL’s parity—exemplified by the fact that eight teams have yet to record a win—means that a single upset can dramatically reshape the playoff landscape.

Looking ahead, Week 3 will be a litmus test for these struggling franchises. A victory for any of the highlighted teams could ignite a momentum shift that carries them through the grueling 17‑game marathon. While the odds remain stacked against them, the combination of emerging talent, strategic coaching tweaks and a comparatively forgiving slate of opponents keeps the Texans, Buccaneers and Colts firmly in the conversation. As the season unfolds, fans of these clubs will be watching closely, hoping that early adversity translates into the kind of resilience that defines playoff teams.
